newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-TIMELINES - Today in History - Feb 3.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-TIMELINES - Today in History - Feb 3.

text.p: BIRTHDAYS
German composer FELIX M*NDELSSOHN-BARTHOLDY, famous for "THE MIDSUMMER NIGHT'S DREAM", was born on this day in 1809.
American writer GERTRUDE STEIN was born in 1874.
The American writer who created 'Hopalong Cassidy', CLARENCE MULFORD, was born in 1883.

Irish entertainer VAL DOONICAN was born on this day in 1929. He began his career on Irish radio in the forties and played with a touring band 'The Four Ramblers' in the fifties. He started a solo career in the late fifties and had his own radio show "A Date with Val". From 1964 to 67 he had five top ten hits in the UK. These were "Walk Tall" (1964), "The Special Years" (1965), "Elusive Butterfly" (1966), "What Would I Be" (1966) and "If The Whole World Stopped Loving"(1967).
Former Australian Test skipper and present Coach, BOB SIMPSON, was born in 1936.
Singer TRISH NOBLE, once PATSY-ANN NOBLE, was born in 1944.

American singer/ songwriter MELANIE SAFKA was born in 1947. Her hits included "Lay Down (Candles In The Rain)" (1970), "Ruby Tuesday" (1970) and "Brand New Key" (1971). She continued making records into the eighties.
EVENTS
1399 : The Duke of Lancaster and Father of England's KING HENRY IV, JOHN of GAUNT, died.
1488 : Portugese explorer BARTHOLOMEU DIAZ became the first European to land on African soil.
1877 : The piece of music "Chopsticks", composed by ARTHUR De LULL (in reality 16 year-old EUPHEMIA ALTEN), was registered at the British Museum.
1919 : The League of Nations (now the United Nations) staged its first meeting in Paris, chaired by United States' President WOODROW WILSON.
1931 : An earthquake struck New Zealand, killing 216 people. 1954 : Thousands of Sydneysiders turned-out to welcome QUEENELIZABETH II and PRINCE PHILLIP on their Royal Tour of Australia.

1959 : It was a day when the rock music industry lost three greats BUDDY HOLLY, BIG BOPPER and RITCHIE VALENS were killed on their way from Clear Lake to their next performance. Their plan crashed a few minutes after takeoff, near Manson City, Iowa.
1960 : British Prime Minister HAROLD MACMILLAN told the South African Parliament during his national tour, that the country should accept racial equality.
1963 : Pop fans snap-up first copies of BUDDY HOLLY's long awaited L-P "REMINISCING", released four years after his death in a plane crash.
1966 : The Soviet unmanned spacecraft "LUNA 4" made the first landing on the moon.
1969 : YASSER ARAFAT took over the leadership of the Palestine Liberation Organisation.
1969 : English horror-movie actor BORIS KARLOFF died at 82.
1977 : Australia had an unemployment rate of 5.8 percent, with more than 350,000 unemployed. It was the highest figure since the depression in the thirties.
1989 : P. W. BOTHA quit as South Africa's ruling party Chief.
1989 : British Telecom banned "chat-lines", admitting that people were getting hooked on the service, and were running-up enormous phone bills.
